exposure: interpregnancy interval ≤6 months after dilation and evacuation
interpregnancy interval >6 months after dilation and evacuation
Interpregnancy interval after dilation and evacuation (D&E) (≤6 months vs. >6 months)
cohort: 214 women who underwent D&E (14-26 weeks) and had a subsequent pregnancy
finding: No significant difference in the rate of preterm birth or other adverse pregnancy outcomes was found between women who conceived within 6 months of D&E and those who conceived more than 6 months after.
mod_finding: This study on interpregnancy intervals after D&E did not find significant differences in mode of delivery between groups.
